# **GAME DESIGN DOCUMENT (GDD)**

## **Working Title: Prison Break**

**Unity Version 2022.3.62f2**

**Video Run through of prototype**  
[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tt5Cj\_wT7cg\&feature=youtu.be](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tt5Cj_wT7cg&feature=youtu.be)

# **1\. High-Level Overview**

## **1.1 Concept Statement**

*Prison Break* is a physics-based puzzle game where players manipulate the **mass and size of their shackles** to navigate through a prison and escape. The design explores the question:

**How does manipulating an object's weight affect problem solving and maneuverability?**

Players control a prisoner bound to a ball-and-chain with the unique ability to expand or shrink the ball’s size and mass. This mechanic is used to overcome physical obstacles, break structures, activate pressure-based devices, and navigate environmental hazards.

## **1.2 Genre**

Puzzle / Physics-Based Adventure

# **2\. Player Experience**

## **2.1 Player Role**

The player is a confined prisoner attempting to escape a fortified prison using only their physics-altering shackles.

**2.2 Player Fantasy**

“I can weaponize the weight of my restraints to break free.”

## **2.3 Desired Emotions**

* Ingenuity

* Tension

* Satisfaction

* Discovery

## **2.4 Perspective**

Third-person or first-person (based on prototype needs).

# **3\. Core Gameplay**

## **3.1 Core Loop**

**Encounter obstacle → Adjust ball mass/size → Apply physics solution → Progress deeper into prison**

## **3.2 Core Mechanic: Mass & Size Manipulation**

### **Effects of Increasing Mass:**

* Slower player movement

* Greater force when swinging

* Can break weak walls

* Holds heavy pressure plates

### **Effects of Reducing Mass:**

* Faster, more agile movement

* Reduced drag and momentum

* Easier to carry/drag over obstacles

### **Effects of Increasing Size:**

* Greater reach for switches

* Stronger push/pull

* Anchors player in place

### **Effects of Decreasing Size:**

* Fit through tight passages

* Minimize collision footprint

* Allows stealthier movement

## **3.3 Movement & Physics**

* Momentum-based swings

* Physics-driven collisions

* Variable jump behavior depending on weight

# **4\. Level Design**

## **4.1 Example Level: Prototype Prison Escape**

1. Begin confined in a cell.

2. Shrink ball to escape through a gap.

3. Enlarge ball to smash a weakened wall.

4. Use increased weight to activate a pressure plate.

5. Cross a pit using momentum swings.

6. Navigate hazardous corridors.

7. Exit the prison.

## **4.2 Level Goals**

* Teach weight manipulation mechanics

* Gradually escalate puzzle complexity

* Encourage experimentation

* Build toward a satisfying escape sequence  
  ![][image1]  
  (Example of level/puzzle designs in concept phase)

# **5\. Game Systems**

## **5.1 Shackle System**

* Ball physics (mass, drag, size)

* Chain physics (dynamic link behavior)

* Collision logic with player & environment

* Visual scaling & audio cues

### ***Prototype Limitation:***

Current chain physics caused erratic behavior when the ball collided with the player or environment. A built-in Unity chain/rope solution might resolve this, but time constraints prevented deeper exploration.

## **5.2 Environmental Systems**

* Breakable surfaces

* Weighted switches

* Movable physics blocks

* Slopes, pits, and uneven terrain

* Hazards (spikes, collapsing floors, security elements)

## **5.3 Feedback Systems**

**Visual:** Ball scales up/down, cracks form on breakable walls  
 **Audio:** Metallic clanks, heavy thuds, dragging

**5.4 Metrics** 

**Prison cell**  
	3m(L) x 3m(W) x 2.4m(H)  
Length & Width dimensions for via wikipedia, average cell dimensions for a jail cell in poland.   
Height wasn’t able to be found, so I plugged the height of the average room.

**Prison fence**  
	12 ft tall (3.6 metres)

Height found via, Rite-Way fencing Inc. website. Listed is the typical height of the average prison fencing in Canada.   
Length is negligible as the fence needs to block the player, will be as long as the room needs it to be

**Prison Weighted Ball & Chain**  
	Approx 4 lbs in weight  
	Chain length 31 in (0.7 m) 

Weight and length found via Atlanta Cutlery.  
The length will likely need to be extended for our level to function as intended, the weight listed can be used as our minimum/baseline

# **6\. Art Direction**

## **6.1 Visual Style**

* Stylized prison environment

* Industrial metal, concrete, and harsh lighting

* Clear visual feedback for mass changes

* Heavy emphasis on materials (metal, stone, debris)

# **7\. Audio Direction**

## **7.1 Sound Design**

* Metal clanking, scraping, and swinging

* Heavy environmental impacts

* Prison ambience: echoes, pipes, guards

**8\. Technical Overview**

## **8.1 Engine**

Unity Version 2022.3.62f2 (focused on physics implementation)

**9.2 Risks & Challenges**

* Chain physics instability

* Weight manipulation causing unexpected forces

* Collision conflicts between player and shackle

* Performance concerns with dynamic physics

# **9\. Summary**

*Prison Break* is a physics-focused puzzle game centered on manipulating the mass and size of a ball-and-chain to escape a hostile prison. While the prototype revealed challenges with chain physics, the core mechanic shows strong potential for creative puzzle solving, player expression, and emergent gameplay.
